missing: HL7 FHIR is absent from all lenses and is the closest LIVING prior art: receiver-published machine-readable profiles (Implementation Guides, StructureDefinition, CapabilityStatement) with executable validators and automated conformance testing (Inferno). It proves the architecture lens's pattern technically works at scale — and simultaneously shows adoption required a regulatory mandate (ONC), profile proliferation re-created variance (US Core vs national IGs), and certification testing persisted anyway. The assessment needs it both as feasibility evidence and as a cautionary control case.

EDIFACT APERAK and X12 824 Application Advice are missing: standardized, machine-readable, IN-BAND business-level rejection messages already exist and are barely implemented. Two lenses claim business rejections travel only by email/phone — incomplete, and the real lesson is stronger: the proposal's 'structured in-band rejection/enrichment' feature has direct prior art that failed commercially, not a gap in the standards.

GS1 GDSN / data pools as prior art: the retail-native precedent for registry-based machine-readable semantics (product master data) at global scale — partially successful, with well-documented data-quality problems, regional profile divergence, and pool fragmentation. All lenses cite GDSN only as out-of-band state; none mine it as the closest retail analogue for the proposed registry.

The LLM counterfactual that undercuts the whole idea: if LLM compilation-with-tests can bind contracts to ERPs, it can equally compile mappings from existing MIG PDFs, Stedi Guides, and sample files against EDIFACT/X12 today — no new wire format required. No lens examines whether AI-assisted mapping over legacy formats (incumbent networks, Osmos/Lume-style startups, Stedi itself) captures the value first and makes the language redundant.

No empirical grounding for the core mechanism: zero data anywhere on LLM auto-mapping accuracy, error rates, or verification cost; and no use of Procuros' own internal data to decompose onboarding cost into mapping vs testing vs process/master-data alignment — the single number that decides how much of the problem self-description can even address. The author can measure this; the assessment should demand it.

In-band change/enrichment requests as a fraud vector: a protocol where counterparty messages auto-update mappings is a BEC/invoice-redirection attack surface (an injected 'change proposal' altering invoicee GLN or payment fields). The adversarial lens covers schema poisoning and DoS but not fraud through the legitimate protocol. Related: most SME endpoints are unattended (run by providers), so in-band negotiation has no responder.

Liability and legal-agreement framework: trading-partner/interchange agreements, who bears the loss when an auto-built mapping mispays, and the evidentiary role of the human-signed spec are unaddressed. Also unflagged: using 'anonymized production traffic as test vectors' and mining customer JSONata mappings raises confidentiality/GDPR/contract-IP problems — real prices, volumes, and trading relationships leak through test vectors.

Operations and correlated failure: a central registry of executable contracts converts today's bilaterally isolated failures into correlated outages — one bad contract version or validator release breaks thousands of flows simultaneously (Peppol/EN 16931 Schematron release regressions are precedent). No lens covers rollback, blast radius, registry availability, or the PKI/trust hierarchy (who plays OpenPeppol's CA role).

Direction asymmetry and long-tail authoring burden: in retail order-to-cash the giant SENDS ORDERS, so a receiver-publishes-contract model requires thousands of small suppliers — today on CSV/PDF/email — to author machine-readable contracts for inbound documents, a capability they demonstrably lack. The lenses discuss retailer incentives but not who authors contracts for the weak side of each flow.

Vendor-seeded standard credibility and self-cannibalization: cXML/Ariba shows network-operator-owned 'open' formats cap out at the operator's walled garden; rival networks (SPS, TrueCommerce, EDICOM, Stedi) won't adopt a Procuros-seeded registry, and a P2P language that eliminates mapping partially disintermediates Procuros' own hub business. Neither the governance path (de facto spec vs multi-year GS1/UN-CEFACT standardization) nor who pays for registry upkeep is analyzed.

Academic schema/ontology-matching literature (OAEI benchmarks, COMA/Cupid lineage): decades of results showing automated matching plateaus well below the accuracy finance-grade documents require — a quantitative bound on 'receivers auto-build mappings' that no lens cites.
contradictions: The five lenses are not assessing the same artifact. The pitch is per-message self-description with mappings auto-built from received messages and in-band change requests; the architecture lens explicitly abandons all three ('never per-message blueprints', pairwise contracts are 'O(N²), EDI's disease restated', canonical semantics survive as a registry). Four lenses refute the pitched idea; the fifth quietly substitutes ebXML-CPP-plus-Peppol-plus-Stedi-Guides with LLM tooling. The final assessment must state explicitly that the pitched form is rejected by convergent evidence and only the registry-contract steelman is defensible — and that the steelman is a different product.

Bilateral testing: architecture claims computed conformance + test vectors + signed attestations eliminate it; adversarial, prior-art (RosettaNet still required certification), and adoption lenses hold that testing establishes trust in money-flows, processes, and master data, which schemas cannot carry, and predict enterprises re-impose certification. Architecture's self-service attestation is exactly the 'sender grading its own homework' the adversarial lens rejects — the lenses never engage on who runs the tests. The assessment must estimate what fraction of testing is spec-conformance (automatable) vs process/data trust (not).

E-invoicing timing: the peppol lens concludes the 2026–2030 format slot is legally pre-awarded to EN 16931 syntaxes and the regulatory tailwind is ABSENT in the open order-to-cash space; the adoption lens recommends 'time launch to the 2026–2030 mandates' as wedge #5. Resolution required: the wave helps only a compliance-adjacent bridge/tooling product, never a rival invoice language — and gives no push in ORDERS/DESADV where the idea actually lives.

Problem-size math is incoherent across lenses: adoption cites $750–2,500 per-partner onboarding (Orderful) and concedes modern pre-mapped platforms already onboard in days; peppol cites $20k–50k VAN EDI setup (Acume, single vendor, one volume tier). An order-of-magnitude spread in the pain being sold, and the 'already solved in days' concession shrinks the pitch's marginal benefit. Normalize scopes (per-partner mapping vs full program setup) or drop the cost framing.

Share of the mapping problem that is machine-addressable: prior-art says self-description 'never' touches the semantic layer; adversarial says it solves syntax fully, schema partially, business semantics not at all; architecture claims LLM-generated mappings plus CEL rules make most of it computable. Three incompatible estimates of the addressable cost — the assessment's verdict hinges on picking one and defending it.

Peppol is used both ways: the peppol lens presents it as the counterexample (variance eliminated by ONE fixed profile — the opposite of self-description); the architecture lens cites SML/SMP as proof registry discovery of receiver capabilities scales. Both facts are true, but SMP publishes pointers into a small closed set of fixed profiles; extrapolating it to open-ended per-receiver contract publication reverses the mechanism that made Peppol work. The assessment must not let the precedent claim stand unqualified.

Related tension worth resolving in the proposal's favor: prior-art says OpenAPI won because one side dictates an executable contract — but retail EDI ALSO has one side dictating (the retailer's MIG). The OpenAPI success conditions are arguably satisfiable in retail if retailers publish executable contracts, which relocates the blocker from technical feasibility to pure incentive (adversarial's point). No lens connects these.

Minor factual harmonization needed: Walmart AS2 savings attribution (adoption summary says savings accrued to Walmart; its own verification note says suppliers also escaped VAN fees); EN 16931 revision dates (peppol: CEN approvals Oct 2025 / 13 Feb 2026 vs adversarial: EN 16931-1:2026 approved 18 Mar 2026 — approval vs publication, pick one framing); EN 16931 rule counts (peppol '955+' vs architecture verification's directly counted ~983 UBL / ~808 CII per syntax).
risky_claims: 'LLM compilation-with-tests removes the manual ERP-binding cost' — the entire 'why now, not 2001' argument. Flagged as inference even in its own verification; no accuracy data, benchmark, pilot, or case study anywhere in five lenses. Must be presented as an untested hypothesis (and the assessment's main recommended experiment), not as a premise.

'Semantic/business-process reconciliation dominates onboarding effort' (adversarial/adoption) and its mirror image in the pitch (mapping dominates) — verdict only 'plausible', purely analytical, yet it is the crux: it determines how much cost self-description can remove. Currently unquantified despite being measurable from Procuros' own onboarding records.

Peppol onboarding economics: '$5–15k vs $20–50k, same-day partner activation' — verdict CORRECTED: figures from one vendor (Acume) at one volume tier; vendor said 'hours to days', not same-day; TradeCentric cites 2–8 weeks setup. Present only as a single vendor's directional claim.

EN 16931 '176 business terms' — CORRECTED to 161 (BT-1..BT-161); '~955 Schematron rules' — CORRECTED to ~983 (UBL) / ~808 (CII) per syntax, and the widely quoted 955+ figure is a single vendor's tally. Fix before publication; these are the kind of checkable numbers that discredit the rest.
QTY+192 as the variable-weight/catch-weight example — REFUTED (6063 code 192 = free goods quantity). Replace with EANCOM variable-measure GTIN + QTY per KGM pattern or drop the example.

France '~101 certified PDPs' — stale (≈147 Plateformes Agréées as of Aug 2026); Germany ZRE/OZG-RE described as per-Bundesland platforms — CORRECTED: both federal, ZRE discontinued end-2025; Länder variance comes from separate state portals.

Peppol scale statistics (1.4–2M registered receivers, ~98 countries, 300+ APs, 6M docs/month, 1,173% growth since 2019) — labeled 'verified-web' in key points but has NO corresponding verification entry in the lens. Treat as unverified OpenPeppol/vendor marketing until sourced.

Tradacoms 'still carries the majority of UK retail EDI traffic' — rests on dated Wikipedia/vendor text, no fresh measurement; keep the qualitative point (thirty-year persistence at named retailers), soften the majority statistic.

Chargeback-profit-center thesis and its sub-numbers: '30–50% of fines disputable' could not be located in cited sources; 'Amazon deductions ~7% of vendor revenue' comes from deduction-recovery vendor marketing (Carbon6/SPS). Directionally useful for the incentive argument but evidentially soft, and retailers publicly frame fines as behavior-shaping, not revenue — present as contested.

Architecture's machine-computed breaking/non-breaking diff classification — the Confluent precedent covers STRUCTURAL compatibility only; semantic changes (meaning shifts with unchanged structure, e.g., net-to-gross price basis) are not machine-classifiable in general. On its face this overclaims exactly where the proposal is weakest.

'Business-level rejections travel only by email/phone/portal' — overstated: EDIFACT APERAK and X12 824 exist in-standard for this. The defensible claim is that they are rarely implemented — which is itself prior art AGAINST the proposal's in-band protocol, not support for its novelty.

Design arithmetic presented with false precision: 50–500KB per-message schema bloat, ~100-byte digests, O(N²) relocation — all 'plausible' analytical estimates. Fine as reasoning; do not cite as measured facts.
notes: Overall shape for the final assessment: the five lenses converge remarkably — self-description reliably kills the syntax layer and never the business-semantics layer, and every fast format reset in history was forced (mandate or dictating giant), never won on merit. But the synthesis must be honest that (a) the only defensible version is the architecture lens's registry-published receiver contracts, which is a materially different product from the pitched per-message self-describing language with auto-built mappings and in-band renegotiation — and that steelman is approximately ebXML CPP + Peppol SMP + Stedi Guides + FHIR IGs with LLM tooling bolted on, so its differentiation rests entirely on the unverified LLM-binding claim; (b) the strongest unexamined objection is the LLM counterfactual — if AI mapping works, it works on legacy EDIFACT/X12 without a new language, which attacks the idea from the opposite side to all five lenses; and (c) the most dangerous pitched feature, in-band change requests auto-updating mappings, doubles as a payment-fraud vector no lens analyzed. Two on-their-face gaps in the steelman worth naming: signed self-attestation does not answer the trust-inversion objection (who executes the conformance tests matters more than the signature), and test vectors derived from real traffic are a confidentiality/GDPR landmine. Recommended empirics before any verdict hardens: decompose Procuros' own onboarding hours into syntax/mapping vs testing vs process-and-master-data alignment, and pilot LLM contract-to-ERP binding with measured error rates — those two numbers decide whether the idea attacks 60% of the cost or 15%.
